title: introduce-temporal-operator-delegation-and-audit-context-consistency
author: Marisol Ortega
release_notes: Add temporal operator delegation tokens with TTL and audit-context consistency across retries; KMS metadata tagging to record region pin; non-breaking opt-in for enterprise tenants via feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Operator-scoped service accounts are widely used by orchestration tooling in Dedicated and Private deployments. We observed two gaps in production audits and compliance reviews: 1) long-lived delegated operator tokens that are hard to attribute and revoke, and 2) audit traces that are fragmented across retry/fanout boundaries and when requests are proxied through intermediate publishers. This PR implements a pragmatic, opt-in operator temporal delegation model (short TTLs + auditable provenance) and a consistent audit-context propagation scheme so that a single logical action keeps a trace ID and KMS provenance tag across retries and internal fanout. This change is targeted at RBAC v2 flows and KMS integration points used by the Private installer and Dedicated agent.

What this changes (high-level):
- Introduce OperatorDelegation record and short-lived delegation tokens (default TTL 1h, configurable per-operator via feature flag and tenant policy). Tokens are minted by the operator-auth service and bound to: operator-id, allowed-action-scopes, creation-ts, expiry-ts, and kms-region-affinity metadata. Token format is JWT-like but signed with our operator attestation key and includes a proof-hash of the backing KMS key (when present).
- Audit context headers: add X-RD-Audit-Trace and X-RD-KMS-Provenance headers. These are injected by the edge proxy and preserved through internal RPCs and message bus fanout. When absent, services now deterministically synthesize a trace and attach provenance if KMS operations occur during the request.
- KMS metadata tagging: when a delegated token is used to perform KMS operations we now emit a kms.provenance tag (region/managed-cmk-id) into the audit envelope. This is recorded by the audit-forwarder and visible in the Console audit search.
- RBAC v2 guard: operator-delegation TTL is enforced during policy evaluation (reject expired delegations). New unit in policy-compiler ensures region affinity constraints cannot be widened by delegation.
- Migration: a background job migrates older operator sessions to explicit operator-delegation records with a default conservative expiry; tenant admins can opt-in to a stricter default via the admin API.
- Operational controls: rollout feature flag (operator.temporal_delegation) and a canary mode that logs but does not enforce expiry to aid rolling upgrades.

Files changed (summary): added new service handlers, policy checks, audit envelope augmentation, docs and tests. See changed_files for a top-level list.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for token issuance/validation, RBAC expiry checks, and an integration test that simulates a proxy -> broker -> worker fanout preserving the trace header. CI initially failed due to a test race with time.Now() in the token-refresh helper; fixed by injecting a monotonic clock in the test harness. All checks green on final push.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag off by default; 2) Enable canary for 10% operator traffic and validate audit continuity via the Console audit viewer (team: infra/sre); 3) After 2 weeks, enable enforcement for canary tenants; 4) Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring of audit reassembly error rate and KMS call attribution metrics.

Related: Linear ENG-4123 (operator delegation), SEC-58 (audit provenance), RFC: docs/rfcs/2024-operator-delegation.md.
